strategy.summary: Reproduce the zero-length-axis defect in xt::roll (xtensor-stack/xtensor PR #2922) at buggy commit 9575b39760960ed624c06367c16315761d7250c7. xt::roll on arrays containing a zero-length axis enters an infinite loop (while (shift < 0) shift += flat_size with flat_size == 0) and then would hit shift %= 0 (UB); the fix in include/xtensor/misc/xmanipulation.hpp adds an early 'if (cpy.size() == 0) return cpy;'. The PR adds shape-checking assertions to test/test_xmanipulation.cpp using xarray<double>::from_shape({0}), {3,0}, {3,0,4}. Success = the new roll assertions never complete (hang/timeout) on the buggy commit, and pass after the fix.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: No value returned: infinite loop at 'while (shift < 0) shift += flat_size' with flat_size == 0 (and shift %= 0 is UB); call hangs
input_output_examples.expected_output: An empty array whose .shape() == empty_1d.shape(), i.e. shape {0}

input_output_examples.buggy_output: No value returned: the axis-1 length is 0, so flat_size/shift math collapses to 0 and the while loop never terminates; call hangs
input_output_examples.expected_output: An array whose .shape() == partial_empty.shape(), i.e. shape {3, 0}

input_output_examples.buggy_output: No value returned: array contains a zero-length axis, flat_size == 0 drives the while (shift < 0) loop to hang (shift %= 0 UB)
input_output_examples.expected_output: An array whose .shape() == mixed_empty.shape(), i.e. shape {3, 0, 4}

C++ compiler with C++14 support (C++17 recommended); xtensor is header-only so no library build is required
CMake >= 3.x, plus the xtl dependency (and xsimd if XTENSOR_USE_XSIMD is enabled) available to the test build
GoogleTest available for the test target (bundled/fetched by xtensor's CMake test configuration)
Outer tooling must impose a wall-clock timeout, since the defect manifests as a hang rather than an assertion mismatch
reproduction_steps: Confirm the working tree is at the buggy commit 9575b39760960ed624c06367c16315761d7250c7 with include/xtensor/misc/xmanipulation.hpp NOT containing the 'if (cpy.size() == 0) return cpy;' guard
Configure and build the test_xmanipulation target as above
Run the roll test in the test_xmanipulation binary (see test_command) under a timeout, e.g. 'timeout 120 ./build/test/test_xmanipulation --gtest_filter=<roll test>'

Observe that the new EXPECT_EQ assertions for xarray<double>::from_shape({0}), {3,0} and {3,0,4} are never reached/reported because xt::roll spins forever in 'while (shift < 0) shift += flat_size;' with flat_size == 0
Record the timeout/hang as the failing behaviour; do not modify source (this task is reproduction only)

strategy.summary: Reproduce a container rank-mismatch buffer overflow in xtensor: assigning a higher-dimensional expression (xt::expand_dims(a, 0), shape {1,2}) to a fixed-rank xtensor<float,1> (shape {2}) overflows the buffer instead of rejecting the assignment. The added test xassign.fixed_dimension_mismatch asserts a std::runtime_error is thrown; on the buggy commit no exception is thrown (release: stack smashing), so the test fails/crashes.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: No std::runtime_error thrown; resize truncates the assignee shape {1,2} -> {1} and then copies 2 elements into a 1-element buffer, causing a buffer overflow / stack smashing (release builds).
input_output_examples.expected_output: A std::runtime_error is thrown because the number of dimensions of the expression (2) does not match the fixed rank of the tensor (1).

environment_setup: Linux x86_64 with a C++14/17 compiler (gcc or clang) and CMake >= 3.x.
Clone the repository and check out the buggy commit 2b01100feae099fe3f9476c62e2f1edebeed9aa5.
Ensure gtest is available (xtensor tests link against googletest); configure with -DXTENSOR_BUILD_TESTS=ON.
Configure a release build (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release / NDEBUG) so the internal XTENSOR_ASSERT is disabled and the overflow is reached instead of trapping early.
build_steps: cmake --build . --target test_xtest -j$(nproc)  (build the gtest suite that contains test/test_xassign.cpp)
reproduction_steps: Apply the reproducing-test diff to the buggy checkout: add `#include "xtensor/misc/xmanipulation.hpp"` to test/test_xassign.cpp and append the TEST(xassign, fixed_dimension_mismatch) block that does `auto a = xt::xtensor<float, 1>::from_shape({2}); XT_ASSERT_THROW(a = xt::expand_dims(a, 0), std::runtime_error);`.
Do NOT modify include/xtensor/containers/xcontainer.hpp — the fix must remain unapplied.
Rebuild the test_xtest target so the new test is compiled into the suite.
Run the gtest filter for the new test and observe the failure/crash at this buggy revision.
Optionally rebuild with AddressSanitizer (-fsanitize=address) to make the buffer overflow explicit instead of a silent stack-smashing abort.
strategy.expected_buggy_behavior: The assignment `a = xt::expand_dims(a, 0)` does not throw std::runtime_error on the buggy commit. The container resizes to a truncated shape and copies the source dimensions into the smaller destination, causing a buffer overflow / stack smashing; XT_ASSERT_THROW fails (or the process aborts) instead of a clean exception.
strategy.expected_fixed_behavior: The number of dimensions is validated before assignment, so `a = xt::expand_dims(a, 0)` throws std::runtime_error; XT_ASSERT_THROW(std::runtime_error) passes and the test succeeds without any memory corruption.
strategy.success_criterion: At buggy commit 2b01100 the test xassign.fixed_dimension_mismatch FAILS — no std::runtime_error is thrown (and/or the process crashes with a buffer overflow) — while at fixed commit 8adbd1c the same test PASSES because the assignment throws std::runtime_error.
risks_or_ambiguities: The test does not exist at the buggy commit; test/test_xassign.cpp must be manually patched with the PR's hunk before the test can be run.
